AgentUsageStats.description: The tool/usage counts a spawn result carries back to the parent.
AgentUsageStats.title: AgentUsageStats

BackgroundJobView.description:
One job's state for ``background_status`` — relative times only (the repo
convention, via ``format_age_ago``), never raw timestamps.
BackgroundJobView.title: BackgroundJobView

background.description: Run this command in the BACKGROUND: return a job id immediately instead of blocking, and notify you with the command's full output when it finishes. Use for a slow, independent command (a build, a full test run, a long-running script, a dev server). Permissions are still checked up front. Don't poll; you'll be notified. Leave false when you need the output for your next step.
background.title: Background

command.description: The command to execute. Runs in a fresh, stateless shell — chain dependent steps in one call with `&&`; set `workdir` instead of `cd`.
command.title: Command

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words.
description.title: Description

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds. The command is killed if it exceeds this. Leave it unset to let the command run as long as it needs; it is then stopped only if it sits idle, printing nothing and using no CPU.
timeout.title: Timeout

workdir.description: The working directory to run the command in (relative to the workspace root, or absolute under it). Defaults to the workspace root. Use this instead of a `cd` in the command — `cd` does not persist.
workdir.title: Workdir

result_name.description: A SHORT, human-friendly name for the result you expect (5 words or fewer, e.g. 'Q3 revenue by region', 'failed login counts'). Always provide it: when the result is large it's stored and shown under this name in the editor, so a good label makes it findable. Describe the result, not the query.
result_name.title: Result Name

result_name.description: A SHORT, human-friendly name for the result you expect (5 words or fewer, e.g. 'Q3 revenue by region', 'failed login counts'). Always provide it: when the result is large it's stored and shown under this name in the editor, so a good label makes it findable. Describe the result, not the query.
result_name.title: Result Name

where.description: A SQL boolean predicate over the columns (e.g. "amount > 100").
where.title: Where

BlobHandle.description:
A pointer to a spilled result in the content-addressed blob store. Handed
to the model / editor in place of an oversized inline payload; dereferenced
via the ``fetch_result`` tool or the ``blob.fetch`` RPC.

Persisted ⇒ ``VersionedModel``: the handle rides a promoted result's spec
into the cloud, so a field a newer daemon adds beside the digest has to
survive an older reader instead of being dropped on the way through.
BlobHandle.title: BlobHandle

filename.description: Optional file name (a single name, no path). The right extension is added automatically; defaults to a name derived from the handle.
filename.title: Filename

path.description: Absolute path to the written file (under the chat sandbox). Run your own code over it — e.g. `python -c "import pandas as pd; df = pd.read_parquet(...)"`. Reference it in a reply by its name relative to the working directory.
path.title: Path

result_name.description: A SHORT, human-friendly name for the result you expect (5 words or fewer, e.g. 'Q3 revenue by region', 'failed login counts'). Always provide it: when the result is large it's stored and shown under this name in the editor, so a good label makes it findable. Describe the result, not the query.
result_name.title: Result Name

CellAfterOp.description:
A cell a batch touched, as it is after the batch.

``index`` is its place among the live cells, ``None`` once it is deleted.
``status`` is its run status when the writer knows it: the engine's client
fills it; a document store, which holds no run state, leaves it ``None``.
CellAfterOp.title: CellAfterOp

CellNotice.description:
Something a reader of the document should know about a cell.

``kind`` is an open string. Core kinds: ``cell_running``,
``edited_deleted_cell``, ``external_conflict``, ``kind_changed_by_other``,
``upstream_being_edited``. The engine also emits ``stale_base``,
``duplicate_name``, ``invalid_file``,
``file_deleted``, ``corrupt_snapshot``, ``memory_warning``.
CellNotice.title: CellNotice

env_path.description: The environment to capture. Leave empty for the active one (in a cloud chat, the environment `python` runs in).
env_path.title: Env Path

dry_run.description: Only plan: list the commands without running any.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

env_path.description: The environment to build or update. Leave empty for the active one (in a cloud chat) or the project's `.venv` (locally).
env_path.title: Env Path

FetchResultOutput.description:
Cursor fields FIRST: when an oversized page rides the generic dispatch
spill, only the head of the serialized result survives as the preview, and
the cursor (``next_offset``/``has_more``) must be in it or paging dead-ends.
Serialization follows this declaration order.
FetchResultOutput.title: FetchResultOutput

Gap.description: Something the recreate cannot (or did not) make match the spec.
Gap.title: Gap

GraphErrorInfo.description:
A problem in the dependency graph: its code (``multiple_definitions``,
``cycle``, ``syntax``, ``delete_nonlocal``, ...), the name it is about,
and the cells it involves. The one graph error model: ``GraphSummary``,
``GraphView``, the cells of a view and the ``graph`` event all carry it.
GraphErrorInfo.title: GraphErrorInfo

GraphSummary.description:
The document graph (current text): for diagnostics only.

``computed`` is false when the writer had no analysis of exactly the state
it answers for (the platform analyses off the hot path, and the ``graph``
event on the notebook channel carries the analysis once it is ready);
``cells`` and ``edges`` are empty then.
GraphSummary.title: GraphSummary

cells.description: The cells to act on, each its id, name, position (Cell 3), first or last. Omit with clear_outputs to clear every cell.
cells.title: Cells

to.description: For move: up, down, top or bottom.
to.title: To

NotebookEditOutput.description:
The engine's result of the batch (each touched cell with its run
status, notices), for ``path``. ``graph`` covers the touched cells and
the edges into and out of them, not the whole notebook.
NotebookEditOutput.title: NotebookEditOutput

NotebookErrorInfo.description:
A cell's error. ``ename`` is the exception class, reduced to a dotted
identifier; the message and traceback are the notebook's own words.
NotebookErrorInfo.title: NotebookErrorInfo

NotebookGuide.description:
The essentials of the ``notebooks`` skill, carried by the first notebook
tool result in a conversation so the agent has them without loading the
skill. ``version`` changes whenever the text does.
NotebookGuide.title: NotebookGuide

action.description: status; interrupt (the running cell); interrupt_all (the running cell, and drop every queued run); restart (clears every value); shutdown (stops the kernel).
action.title: Action

NotebookMore.description: The call that returns what a result left out, ready to send as is.
NotebookMore.title: NotebookMore

meta.description: Cell settings the file records; for a SQL cell: output_var, connection, engine, show_output.
meta.title: Meta

cell.description: A cell: its id, its name, its position (Cell 3), first or last.
cell.title: Cell

NotebookPage.description: Where a page sits in its list.
NotebookPage.title: NotebookPage

sql_row_limit.description: The most rows kept from a SQL query that has no LIMIT of its own.
sql_row_limit.title: Sql Row Limit

cell.description: A cell: its id, its name, its position (Cell 3), first or last.
cell.title: Cell

NotebookStoredChart.description:
A chart too large to carry in the reply, by the file the notebook keeps
its spec in beside itself (``<sha256>.json`` in the notebook's output
folder): where a chat or a thread reads the spec to draw it.
NotebookStoredChart.title: NotebookStoredChart

NotebookTextPage.description: Where a window of text sits in the whole text.
NotebookTextPage.title: NotebookTextPage

PluginConnectionInfo.description:
A connection a plugin manages, for the agent's discovery tool — live
(``added``) or merely detected (a candidate the user can enable).
PluginConnectionInfo.title: PluginConnectionInfo

PluginInfo.description: One plugin's status for the agent's ``list_plugins`` discovery tool.
PluginInfo.title: PluginInfo

RunAbove.description: Every cell above this one in notebook order (not the cell itself).

id.description: A cell: its id, its name, its position (Cell 3), first or last.
id.title: Id

RunAbove.title: RunAbove

restart.description: Restart the kernel first, so every cell runs from a clean state.
restart.title: Restart

RunBelow.description: This cell and every cell below it in notebook order.

id.description: A cell: its id, its name, its position (Cell 3), first or last.
id.title: Id

RunBelow.title: RunBelow

RunCells.description: These cells, after any cell they need that has not run yet.

ids.description: A cell: its id, its name, its position (Cell 3), first or last.
ids.title: Ids

RunCells.title: RunCells

RunDownstream.description: This cell and every cell that reads it, in either reactivity mode.

id.description: A cell: its id, its name, its position (Cell 3), first or last.
id.title: Id

RunDownstream.title: RunDownstream

RunStale.description: Every cell whose result no longer matches its code or inputs.
RunStale.title: RunStale

RunUpstream.description: This cell and every cell it depends on, run again even when they hold values.

id.description: A cell: its id, its name, its position (Cell 3), first or last.
id.title: Id

RunUpstream.title: RunUpstream

SetCellConfigOp.description:
marimo's cell options, for any cell: ``disabled``, ``hide_code``,
``expand_output``, ``column``. A SQL cell's ``show_output``,
``output_var`` and ``connection`` are not here: they are ``set_meta``.

config.description: Only disabled, hide_code, expand_output or column; SQL settings are set_meta.
config.title: Config

SetCellConfigOp.title: SetCellConfigOp

SetCellMetaOp.description:
A SQL or Markdown cell's settings: for SQL ``connection`` (the name of
one of the workspace's connections; ``None`` runs it in the notebook's
DuckDB), ``output_var`` and ``show_output``; for Markdown ``quote``.
Keys not named keep their value.

meta.description: SQL: connection, output_var, show_output, engine. Markdown: quote.
meta.title: Meta

SetCellMetaOp.title: SetCellMetaOp

SqlProvenance.description:
Where a SQL result came from, beside the rows it describes.

Rendered inline on the result card — never behind a click — and copied onto
the receipt when the result is promoted. Names only: the connection, the
credential role the statement ran under, the engine. A secret never rides
here, and the connector that fills it never sees one.
SqlProvenance.title: SqlProvenance

SqlQueryResult.description:
The shared tabular result shape every rows producer returns, so the
editor chip and ``fetch_result`` paging are identical for every producer.
SqlQueryResult.title: SqlQueryResult

TaskUpsert.description:
One add-or-edit. A new ``id`` creates (``title`` required); an existing ``id``
edits only the fields provided here.

depends_on.description: Ids of prerequisite tasks (replaces the current list).
depends_on.title: Depends On

id.description: Stable slug; new id = create, existing id = edit.
id.title: Id

TaskUpsert.title: TaskUpsert

TaskView.description:
A task as the model sees it — full detail + derived blocked state +
RELATIVE updated time (never a raw timestamp).
TaskView.title: TaskView

ToolCard.description: A discovered tool's advertised shape (what ``search_tools`` returns).
ToolCard.title: ToolCard

Untrusted.description:
Text a notebook produced, carried as data.

``author`` names who caused the text to exist (the person or agent whose run
printed it, or whose edit wrote the source) so the reader can weigh it;
``content`` is the text itself, or for structured outputs (a chart spec, a
table page) the JSON value.
Untrusted.title: Untrusted
